title: Locally of finite type lifts along finite order thickenings (cartesian case)
statement: Let $S\subseteq S'$ be a finite order thickening of schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (a closed subscheme whose quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_{S'}$ satisfies $\mathcal I^{n+1}=0$ for some $n\ge0$), let $f':X'\to S'$ be a morphism of schemes and let $f:X=S\times_{S'}X'\to S$ be its base change [def-pc-base-change]. Then $f$ is locally of finite type if and only if $f'$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. (Affine-locally, by induction on $n$ reducing to $I^2=0$: if $A'\to B'$ is a ring map, $I\subseteq A'$ an ideal with $I^2=0$, and $A'/I\to B'/IB'$ is of finite type, then $A'\to B'$ is of finite type, by Nakayama's lemma applied to $A'[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to B'$ lifting a surjection $(A'/I)[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to B'/IB'$.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW (label lemma-thicken-property-morphisms-cartesian), part (2), with the first three paragraphs of its proof (base change direction; induction on the order of the thickening; reduction to affines) and 'The translation of (2) into algebra' (Nakayama, Algebra Lemma 00DV)

proof.text: ($f'$ locally of finite type $\Rightarrow$ $f$ locally of finite type.) $f:X=S\times_{S'}X'\to S$ is the base change of $f'$ along $i_S:S\to S'$ [def-pc-base-change], and the base change of a morphism locally of finite type is locally of finite type (Morphisms, Lemma 01T4) [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. It remains to prove the converse.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW, proof, first paragraph ('The properties ... are all stable under base change ... Morphisms, Lemma base-change-finite-type') and second paragraph ('The interesting direction ...')

proof.text: (Reduction to affines.) Let $p:X\to X'$ and $q:X\to S$ be the projections, so $f=q$ and $f'\circ p=i_S\circ f$. Let $U'=\operatorname{Spec}A'\subseteq S'$ be an affine open and $V'=\operatorname{Spec}B'\subseteq X'$ an affine open with $f'(V')\subseteq U'$. Put $I=\mathcal I(U')\subseteq A'$, where $\mathcal I$ is the ideal sheaf of $S\subseteq S'$; then $U:=i_S^{-1}(U')$ is an open subscheme of $S$ and $U\to U'$ is identified with $\operatorname{Spec}(A'/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}A'$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and $I^{n+1}=\mathcal I^{n+1}(U')=0$ since $\mathcal I^{n+1}=0$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening, def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Put $W:=p^{-1}(V')\subseteq X$, an open subscheme. Since $i_S(f(W))=f'(p(W))\subseteq U'$, we have $f(W)\subseteq U$, i.e. $W\subseteq q^{-1}(U)$, so $W=q^{-1}(U)\cap p^{-1}(V')$; by the open-subscheme property of fibre products (Schemes, Lemma 01JR) [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] applied to the opens $U\subseteq S$, $V'\subseteq X'$, $U'\subseteq S'$, the canonical morphism $U\times_{U'}V'\to X$ is an open immersion with image $W$, compatibly with the projections. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] (Schemes, Lemma 01I4/01JQ) $U\times_{U'}V'\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A'/I\otimes_{A'}B')$, with the projection to $U$ being $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $A'/I\to A'/I\otimes_{A'}B'$; and $A'/I\otimes_{A'}B'\cong B'/IB'$ via $\bar a\otimes b\mapsto \overline{ab}$ (right exactness of $-\otimes_{A'}B'$ applied to $I\to A'\to A'/I\to0$; elementary). Hence $W$ is an affine open of $X$, $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B'/IB')$, $f(W)\subseteq U$, and the ring map $\mathcal O_S(U)\to\mathcal O_X(W)$ induced by $f$ is the map $A/I\to B'/IB'$ induced by $A'\to B'$ (with $A/I$ meaning $A'/I$). This is the diagram of the source with exact rows $0\to IB'\to B'\to B'/IB'\to0$, $0\to I\to A'\to A'/I\to0$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW, proof, fourth paragraph ('Most of the proofs will use a reduction to the affine case. Let U' ⊂ S' be an affine open ... Then V' ∩ X = Spec(B'/IB') ...')

proof.text: ($f$ locally of finite type $\Rightarrow$ $f'$ locally of finite type.) Assume $f$ is locally of finite type, and let $U'=\operatorname{Spec}A'$, $V'=\operatorname{Spec}B'$ be any affine opens of $S'$, $X'$ with $f'(V')\subseteq U'$. With the notation of step 2, $U\subseteq S$ and $W\subseteq X$ are affine opens with $f(W)\subseteq U$, so by Morphisms 01T2 ((1)$\Rightarrow$(2)) [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] the ring map $A'/I\to B'/IB'$ is of finite type. As $I^{n+1}=0$, the ring lemma [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-lift-nilpotent] (Nakayama's lemma, Algebra 00DV, applied to $A'[x_1,\dots,x_m]\to B'$ lifting generators of $B'/IB'$) gives that $A'\to B'=\mathcal O_{S'}(U')\to\mathcal O_{X'}(V')$ is of finite type. Since $U'$, $V'$ were arbitrary, $f'$ is locally of finite type by 01T2 ((2)$\Rightarrow$(1)) [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]. (The source first reduces, by induction on the order of the thickening along the filtration $S=S_1\subseteq\dots\subseteq S_{n+1}=S'$, to $I^2=0$; this is not needed here, since the ring lemma, like Nakayama's lemma 00DV (11) on which it rests, holds for any nilpotent $I$.) With step 1: $f$ is locally of finite type iff $f'$ is.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 09ZW (more-morphisms.tex:334ff) part (2) and its proof, Morphisms 01T2/01T4 and Algebra 00DV. Statement kept. Proof in three steps: (1) easy direction by base change (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change = locallyOfFiniteType_isStableUnderBaseChange); (2) affine reduction: for affine U'=Spec A' ⊆ S', V'=Spec B' ⊆ X' over it, p^{-1}(V') = U ×_{U'} V' = Spec(B'/IB') over U = Spec(A'/I) (existing leaves lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra; ideal-sheaf definitions); (3) converse by 01T2 (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs = locallyOfFiniteType_iff, Mathlib's definition) and the new unsplit ring lemma lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-lift-nilpotent (A'/I → B'/IB' finite type, I nilpotent ⇒ A' → B' finite type; Nakayama 00DV (11), absent from Mathlib). The source's induction on the order of the thickening is bypassed since 00DV (11) and hence the ring lemma hold for any nilpotent ideal; the affine-open correspondence 06AD and the thickening X ⊆ X' are not needed (the affine open W is a fibre product of affines). Mathlib: only the base change direction is there.
